newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Budgens sales growth ahead.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Budgens sales growth ahead.

text.p: British supermarket group Budgens Plc is in "very good shape" with sales growth ahead of the market and improving operating profit margins, chief executive John von Spreckelsen told Reuters on Monday.

"We are in very good shape as a business. We are growing faster than the market...and we have also been able, in what the industry describes as a fiercely competitive market, to increase our operating profit margins from 3.3 percent to 3.6," he said.
Von Spreckelsen said overall market sales growth in groceries was around three percent compared to a rise of 7.2 percent in Budgens' total sales in the year ending April 27.
Budgens saw pre-tax profits jump nearly 20 percent to 9.07 million stg and paid out a total dividend of 1.4 pence per share, up from 1.25 pence.

Budgens is a medium-sized supermarket chain that focuses on fresh food, service and value-for-money on a local basis, with store sizes averaging 2,000-10,000 square feet compared with around 30,000 square feet for the larger chains.
Von Spreckelsen said the company was seeing price decreases of around one percent currently but had still been able to maintain operating margins at around 3.6 percent.
He said Budgens planned to roll out its joint petrol forecourt shops with Kuwait Petroleum Corp at the rate of one a week starting next year, with around 40 sites planned.
"That's a very exciting development for us," he said.
Budgens also has similar stores in a venture with BP, which launched a venture in September 1996 with rival supermarket Safeway to develop 100 sites to be "food and fuel" stores.
Budgens also has its own credit card, launched with a U.S. company, but has "no intentions of becoming a bank, we think we're too small for that," Von Spreckelsen said.
He said the "existing estate is performing better," pointing to a 2.4 percent rise in sales per square foot in the last year.
"We have enough growth opportunities as a business," he added, pointing to growth in existing stores, new stores and in partnership "with our oil company partners."
He said capital expenditure during the current year would be 18-20 million stg, with the bulk of that going into new stores and refurbishments.
He said the current situation of price decreases, or deflation, retailers had to force suppliers into price cuts.
"Obviously we have been quite successful in doing this last year because that's largely the reason why our operating margins have improved," Von Spreckelsen said.
